slides.headline: On this day, India got its 27th state - and it took seven more years to get its own name back.
Uttarakhand was carved out of Uttar Pradesh on November 9, 2000.
slides.body: Formed under the Uttar Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2000, the new state capped decades of a grassroots hill-state movement rooted in the distinct geography and economy of the Garhwal and Kumaon regions, versus the UP plains.

slides.headline: It was first named Uttaranchal - and renamed Uttarakhand on January 1, 2007.
slides.body: The rename followed sustained public demand to restore the region's historic name. Dehradun became the state capital, and November 9 is now marked every year as Uttarakhand Diwas.

slides.eyebrow: Why it matters for Viksit Bharat 2047
slides.headline: A Viksit Bharat is built state by state, each shaped to fit the people it actually serves.
slides.body: Uttarakhand's creation was a bet that a hill region with its own needs would develop faster as its own state than as a distant corner of a much larger one - a bet the state's growth since has largely paid off.
